statement: We leave open the question whether any two straight-line drawings of the same plane graph G can be morphed so that every intermediate drawing has polynomial size (e.g., the ratio between the length of any two edges is polynomial in the size of G during the entire morph). In order to solve this problem positively, our approach seems to be better than previous ones; intuitively, subgraph removals are more suitable than vertex contractions for a morphing algorithm that doesn’t blow up the size of the intermediate drawings. Nevertheless, we haven’t yet been able to prove that polynomial-size morphs always exist.
